BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF                                       )
EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR                                              ) Docket No. 25-00082-UT
REVISION OF ITS RETAIL ELECTRIC RATES                                     )
PURSUANT TO ADVICE NOTICE NO. 317                                         )

                ORDER ESTABLISHING REVISED PROCEDURAL SCHEDULE
                     AND ADDRESSING OUTSTANDING MOTIONS

           THIS MATTER comes before hearing examiners Keven Gedko and Nicholas Rossi, upon

the Completeness Report filed by the Public Interest Advocacy Staff (“Staff”) of the New Mexico

Public Regulation Commission (“Commission”) on August 12, 2026, and the conclusion of the

Scheduling Conference that was conducted on August 25, 2026. Being duly informed, the Hearing

Examiners FIND and CONCLUDE:

           1.          On July 17, 2026, Hearing Examiner Jocelyn Barrett issued the Sua Sponte Order

Vacating Procedural Schedule, Tolling Pending Deadlines, and Requiring the Filing of an

Amended Application (“Sua Sponte Order”). The Sua Sponte Order vacated the hearing and

procedural schedule previously established, tolled all pending motion and other deadlines, and

required EPE to file, within twenty-one calendar days, a single amended and restated Application

and complete supporting filing package (“Amended Application”).1

           2.          The Sua Sponte Order also required Staff to file a Completeness Report, within

seven calendar days after EPE filed its Amended Application, stating whether the Amended

Application and supporting materials are sufficiently complete, coherent, internally consistent, and

technically usable to permit this proceeding to continue.2

           3.          The Sua Sponte Order established that if Staff concluded that the Amended



1
    Sua Sponte Order (July 16, 2026) at 1, and Decretal ¶¶ A through E.
2
    Id Decretal ¶ F.
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Establishing Revised Procedural Schedule                Docket No. 25-00082-UT



Application is complete, coherent, internally consistent, and sufficiently usable, and the Hearing

Examiner agrees, the Hearing Examiner will issue a new procedural order establishing dates that

are consistent with the then-applicable statutory suspension period, unless the Commission

separately extends the period pursuant to Section 62-8-7(C) NMSA 1978.3

           4.          Further, the Sua Sponte Order established that a new procedural order would

include deadlines and procedures for resolving The City of Las Cruces’ Verified Motion to

Dismiss El Paso Electric Company’s Application for Revision of Retail Electric Rates (“CLC

Motion to Dismiss”), The City of Las Cruces’ Motion for an Order Compelling El Paso Electric

Company to Provide Responses to Discovery Requests and Tolling the Procedural Order’s

Deadlines for Intervenor and Staff Direct Testimony and Rebuttal Testimony (“CLC Motion to

Compel”), and the Expedited Joint Objection and Motion for an Order Rejecting El Paso Electric

Company’s Second Notice of Errata and Staying the Procedural Schedule Pending the Company’s

Compliance with NMPRC Rule 1.2.2.10(G) NMAC (“Joint Objection”).4

           5.          Staff, having reviewed EPE’s Amended Application, has opined that the Amended

Application is sufficiently complete to allow this matter to proceed.5 The Hearing Examiners

agree.

           6.          A scheduling conference was held on August 25, 2026. Representatives of EPE,

Staff, the New Mexico Department of Justice, the City of Las Cruces, Doña Ana County, New

Mexico State University, the Coalition for Clean Affordable Energy, Western Resource

Advocates, The US Department of Defense and all other Federal Executive Agencies, Walmart,

3
    Id Decretal ¶ J.
4

5
    Completeness Report (August 13, 2026) at 7-8.

                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Establishing Revised Procedural Schedule                Docket No. 25-00082-UT



Phillip B. Simpson, and Stephen Fischmann were in attendance.

       7.     At the scheduling conference a revised procedural schedule, the need for any

additional notice, and the status and currentness of the CLC Motion to Dismiss, the CLC Motion

to Compel, and the Joint Objection, were all discussed.

       8.     Based upon the discussion at the scheduling conference, the Hearing Examiners

and the parties came to agreement on a revised schedule for the filing of direct and rebuttal

testimony, and for the public hearing on this matter. The Hearing Examiners also determined that:

                      a. EPE, and any other party besides CLC, shall have an opportunity to

                          respond to CLC’s Motion to Dismiss on or before September 8, 2026.

                      b. The relief requested in the Joint Objection has been granted in this

                          docket, and the Joint Objection is therefore moot.

                      c. The CLC Motion to Compel is no longer current, and any issues

                          addressed in CLC’s Motion to Compel that a party determines to require

                          further consideration, should be addressed in a new filing that reflects

                          the current circumstances and status of discovery matters in this docket.

                          Therefore, the CLC Motion to Compel is moot.

                      d. Notice of the Amended Application should be conducted via publication

                          on EPE’s website and through a social media campaign conducted by

                          EPE, and that notice should clearly identify that EPE’s Amended

                          Application is an amendment to EPE’s previously noticed Application,

                          and is not the filing of a distinct application for an increase in rates.




                                                -3-
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Establishing Revised Procedural Schedule                Docket No. 25-00082-UT



        It is therefore ORDERED:

        A.      The Joint Objection is MOOT.

        B.      The CLC Motion to Compel is MOOT.

        C.      Responses to CLC’s Motion to Dismiss shall be filed on or before September 8,

2026. Staff may file a response, but is no longer required to file a response.6

        D.      All parties have an ongoing obligation to respond to discovery as required by

Commission rules.

        E.      On or before September 3, 2026, EPE shall file a proposed form of website notice

for the Amended Application, and in that filing shall describe the manner in which EPE will

conduct a social media campaign for that notice, including a description of how the social media

campaign will connect customers to the form of notice that will be made available on EPE’s

website.

        F.      On or before September 10, 2026, parties may file comments on EPE’s proposed

form of website notice and EPE’s filed plan for its social media campaign.

        G.      The Hearing Examiners shall issue an Order confirming and/or defining the final

form of website notice, and social media campaign, on or before September 15, 2026.

        H.      The intervention deadline for this docket is extended until October 16, 2026.

Anyone desiring to become a party (“intervenor”) to this case must file a motion for leave to

intervene in conformity with the Commission’s Rules of Procedure 1.2.2.23(A) and 1.2.2.23(B)

NMAC on or before October 16, 2026.

        I.      Staff shall, and any intervenors may, file direct testimony by October 23, 2026.


6
 The Order Requiring EPE and Staff Response to Motion to Dismiss and Extending Deadline for Responses, issued
on July 8, 2026, had previously required Staff to respond to the CLC Motion to Dismiss.

                                                     -4-
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Establishing Revised Procedural Schedule                Docket No. 25-00082-UT



        J.      Any rebuttal testimony shall be filed on or before November 20, 2026.

        K.      Any stipulation and supporting documents pursuant to 1.2.2.20 NMAC shall be

filed on or before December 3, 2026. Additional procedures will be set by separate order if a

stipulation is filed.

        L.      Any motions with respect to testimony, including motions in limine, and motions

to strike testimony, shall be filed on or before November 30, 2026. Responses to such motions

shall be filed on or before December 3, 2026.

        M.      A public hearing shall begin on December 9, 2026, and continue through

December 22, 2026, beginning each day at 9:00 a.m. Mountain Time, via the Zoom video-

conferencing platform. The hearing may be vacated if deemed unnecessary. See 17.1.2.8(C)(3)

NMAC. The hearing will be livestreamed on YouTube and will be displayed on the Commission’s

website at https://www.prc.nm.gov/public-hearings/.

        N.      All parts of the Procedural Order issued on April 27, 2026, that were not modified

by the Second Procedural Order issued on June 22, 2026, and that are not modified by this Order

Establishing a Revised Procedural Schedule and Addressing Outstanding Motions, are in full

force and effect

        O.      All parts of the Second Procedural Order issued on June 22, 2026, are in full force

and effect.




                                                -5-
                   BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Establishing Revised Procedural Schedule                Docket No. 25-00082-UT



      ISSUED under the seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, on August 27, 2026.
